bull.b: A focused pipeline targeting B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases gives Cabaletta a coherent development strategy and exposure to substantial unmet medical needs. Progress across lupus, myositis, and systemic sclerosis could support differentiated positioning if clinical development succeeds.

Relatively modest debt compared with equity limits balance-sheet leverage and reduces fixed financing pressure during development. The rebound in equity also improves solvency and gives management greater flexibility to fund clinical programs and operations.

The substantial warrant exercise proceeds provide a meaningful capital infusion for ongoing development programs and operating needs. This strengthens near-term financial flexibility and may reduce immediate dependence on additional financing while clinical work continues.

bear.b: Cabaletta has no approved products or recurring product revenue, so its business currently lacks commercial cash inflows. Future funding and value creation therefore depend heavily on successful clinical development, regulatory progress, and eventual product launches.

The multi-year expansion in net losses shows that operating costs are rising substantially ahead of commercialization. Persistent losses reduce retained resources and increase the amount of capital required to advance the pipeline before any product revenue can offset expenses.

Cash generation remains a major structural weakness because operating and free cash flow have deteriorated sharply over time. With losses translating into real cash burn, the company is likely to require continued external financing to sustain research and operations.
